scenes.headline: Is South Africa Africa's richest country?
scenes.body: 1st… or 6th? It depends how you measure.
scenes.voiceover: Is South Africa Africa's richest country? It can be first, or sixth. It depends on what you measure. Today we test four measures, using the latest published data. The years differ by measure, and each one is shown on screen.

scenes.headline: Income · Millionaires · Wellbeing · Fairness
scenes.body: Latest published data. Years differ by measure and are shown on screen.
scenes.voiceover: Average income per person. The number of dollar millionaires. Human development. And how evenly income is shared.

scenes.headline: Seychelles leads
scenes.receipt: World Bank WDI, July 2026: GNI per capita 2025, Atlas method
scenes.voiceover: Round one: average income per person, per year, for twenty twenty-five. The World Bank puts Seychelles first, at nineteen thousand two hundred US dollars. It is Africa's only high-income economy.

scenes.headline: Mauritius is second

stat.label: per person, 2025 · 1st after adjusting for local prices

scenes.receipt: World Bank WDI, July 2026: GNI per capita 2025, Atlas method; PPP series
scenes.voiceover: Mauritius is second, at fourteen thousand and forty dollars. Adjust for what money actually buys locally, and Mauritius edges ahead of Seychelles.

scenes.headline: 3. Gabon
scenes.receipt: World Bank WDI, July 2026: GNI per capita 2025, Atlas method
scenes.voiceover: Third is Gabon, at seven thousand five hundred and thirty dollars, an economy built largely on oil.

scenes.headline: 4. Botswana
scenes.receipt: World Bank WDI, July 2026: GNI per capita 2025, Atlas method
scenes.voiceover: Fourth is Botswana, at seven thousand three hundred and ninety dollars, with diamonds at the centre of its economy.

scenes.headline: 5. Libya
scenes.receipt: World Bank WDI, July 2026: GNI per capita 2025, Atlas method
scenes.voiceover: Fifth is Libya, at seven thousand two hundred and fifty dollars, also driven by oil.

scenes.eyebrow: Round 1 result · World Bank WDI, July 2026: GNI per capita 2025, Atlas method
scenes.headline: South Africa is 6th on income per person
scenes.voiceover: South Africa comes sixth, at six thousand two hundred and seventy dollars a year. On income per person, the two island nations lead.

scenes.headline: South Africa leads by far
scenes.receipt: New World Wealth, Africa Wealth Report 2026 (June 2026)
scenes.voiceover: Round two: the number of dollar millionaires. That means people with at least one million US dollars they could invest, not counting their main home. On this count, South Africa leads by a wide margin: forty-eight thousand two hundred millionaires, one hundred and thirty-one people worth over a hundred million dollars, and ten billionaires, as at June twenty twenty-six. This is a total, not a per-person figure, so larger economies naturally count more.

scenes.headline: Almost 4 in 10 of Africa's millionaires

stat.label: of Africa's millionaires live in South Africa

scenes.receipt: New World Wealth, Africa Wealth Report 2026 (June 2026)
scenes.voiceover: That is thirty-eight percent of all the dollar millionaires in Africa.

scenes.headline: 2. Egypt
scenes.receipt: New World Wealth, Africa Wealth Report 2026 (June 2026)
scenes.voiceover: Egypt is second, with fifteen thousand one hundred.

scenes.headline: 3. Morocco
scenes.receipt: New World Wealth, Africa Wealth Report 2026 (June 2026)
scenes.voiceover: Morocco is third, with eight thousand three hundred, just ahead of Nigeria.

scenes.headline: 4. Nigeria
scenes.receipt: New World Wealth, Africa Wealth Report 2026 (June 2026)
scenes.voiceover: Nigeria is fourth, with eight thousand one hundred, its first rise since twenty twenty-one.

scenes.headline: 5. Kenya
scenes.receipt: New World Wealth, Africa Wealth Report 2026 (June 2026)
scenes.voiceover: And Kenya is fifth, with six thousand five hundred. On millionaire numbers, the large mainland economies lead.

scenes.headline: Turning wealth into health and education
scenes.body: The UN's Human Development Index combines life expectancy, schooling and income on a scale of 0 to 1.
scenes.voiceover: Round three: human development. The United Nations' Human Development Index combines life expectancy, schooling and income, on a scale from zero to one. It asks whether wealth turns into longer, better-educated lives.

scenes.eyebrow: Round 3 result · UNDP Human Development Report 2025 (2023 data)
scenes.headline: Seychelles and Mauritius lead · SA 6th
scenes.voiceover: Seychelles leads at zero point eight four eight, followed by Mauritius at zero point eight zero six. They are the only two African countries in the UN's top tier, above zero point eight. Algeria, Egypt and Tunisia follow. South Africa is sixth, at zero point seven four one.

scenes.eyebrow: Round 4 · How evenly income is shared
scenes.headline: A check, not a race
scenes.body: Gini index: 0 = everyone has the same · 100 = one person has everything. Lower is more equal.
scenes.receipt: World Bank Poverty & Inequality Platform (SA survey 2022)
scenes.voiceover: Round four is a check, not a race: how evenly income is shared. The Gini index runs from zero, where everyone has the same, to one hundred, where one person has everything. Here, lower means more equal. South Africa scores fifty-four point one, among the highest in the world. So South Africa ranks high on millionaires, and also high on inequality. Both are true at the same time.

scenes.headline: No country wins every round
scenes.body: SA: 1st on millionaires · 6th on income and human development.
scenes.voiceover: So, is South Africa Africa's richest country? On millionaires, yes, by far. On average income and human development, it is sixth, behind Seychelles and Mauritius. No single country wins every round. It depends on what you measure.

scenes.headline: A country's average is not your number
scenes.body: Your own measure: income, savings and debt. Which round matters most to you? Comment 1, 2, 3 or 4.
scenes.voiceover: And one lesson for your own money. A country's average describes the country, not your household. Your own measure is your income, your savings, and your debt. Which round matters most to you? Tell us in the comments: one, two, three, or four.
